title: Double Column Band Saws — Heavy-Duty Industrial Bandsaws | NovoTech
meta_description: Heavy-duty double column band saws from Ø13″ to 87″ (330–2200 mm): BMSY C semi-automatics, CGH / DG NC miter saws, BMSO CS / CGS servo saws, the XS line, the 600 m/min TERRA 6 and the GANTRY 2200XS.
intro: For heavy bar, billets, beams and bundles the bow runs between two hardened columns instead of pivoting, so the blade enters the material squarely and stays square through the cut. Bekamak builds semi-automatic and fully automatic versions, miter heads to 60°, servo feeding with NC job lists, the enclosed high-tech XS production saws, the high-speed TERRA 6 that runs its blade at up to 1,970 ft/min (600 m/min), the BMSO 1313CS for 51″ blocks and the gantry-type GANTRY 2200XS — from Ø13″ to Ø87″ (330–2200 mm). Known as double column, twin-column or dual column metal bandsaws, these horizontal band saw machines are the industrial choice for heavy solids, bundles and plate.

faq_title: Questions we get asked about Bekamak double-column band saws

faq.q: Why choose a double-column saw over a pivot saw?
faq.a: Rigidity and capacity. The bow is guided on two columns, so there is no side load on the blade — cuts stay square in large solids and the blade lasts longer. Double-column saws also reach capacities a pivot bow cannot: Ø13″ (330 mm) up to Ø87″ (2200 mm) on the Bekamak range, with the GANTRY 2200XS at the top.

faq.q: Can a double-column saw cut miters?
faq.a: Yes — the BMSY CGH (single miter) and BMSY DG NC (double miter) swivel the whole bow assembly up to 60° under hydraulic or NC control, and the automatic CGS/CDGS NC models do the same with servo feeding.
The SV versions of the BMSY C saws have a second vise jaw close to the blade, so short pieces and remnants are clamped on both sides of the cut — useful for cutting slices from blocks and billets.
Bekamak's high-tech production saws: servo-driven bow feed and material feed, full enclosure and CNC control, designed for carbide blades, the fastest cycle times and unattended running.

faq.q: What is different about the TERRA 6?
faq.a: Blade speed. A conventional band saw runs at up to 395 ft/min (120 m/min); the TERRA 6 runs its 2-5/8″ band at up to 1,970 ft/min (600 m/min) on a 40 HP motor, so with the right carbide blade a Ø16-3/8″ (415 mm) solid bar that takes about 22 minutes on a conventional saw is cut in about 2 minutes. A load cell and a deflection sensor let the PC-based control correct the cutting parameters in real time, and the enclosed cabin, zero-remnant unloading and camera are built for unattended production of Ø26″ (660 mm) stock.

It cuts rounds from Ø20″ to Ø87″ (500–2200 mm) and blocks up to 94-1/2″ × 87″, pieces up to 23 ft (7 m) long and 50,000 kg, on a gantry frame 49 ft long — a saw for forges, steel mills and service centres that cut ingots and large billets. Servo bow and material feed, a 40 HP main motor and MES production software are standard.
